conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Electron Filling Principles

summaryBox.title: Electronic Fill Rules
summaryBox.takeaway: Aufbau (n+l energy order), Pauli (no two e⁻ have identical 4 quantum numbers), Hund (singly occupy degenerate orbitals with parallel spins first).

conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Aufbau Principle & $(n+l)$ Madelung Rule**:
• Rule 1: Subshells fill in order of increasing $(n+l)$ value (e.g., $4s$ $[4+0=4]$ fills before $3d$ $[3+2=5]$).
• Rule 2: If $(n+l)$ is identical, lower $n$ subshell has lower energy and fills first (e.g., $3d$ $[3+2=5]$ fills before $4p$ $[4+1=5]$).

$$\text{Energy Order: } 1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p < 4s < 3d < 4p < 5s < 4d < 5p < 6s < 4f < 5d < 6p < 7s < 5f < 6d < 7p$$

2. **Pauli Exclusion Principle**: No two electrons in an atom can possess identical sets of all four quantum numbers ($n, l, m_l, m_s$). An orbital holds a maximum of 2 electrons with opposite spins.
3. **Hund's Rule of Maximum Multiplicity**: Degenerate orbitals are singly occupied with parallel spins before pairing begins.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
EXCHANGE ENERGY COMPARISON (3d⁴ 4s² vs 3d⁵ 4s¹)
                       
   Configuration 1 (3d⁴ 4s²): n = 4 ⟹ E_ex = [4(3)/2] K = 6K
   Configuration 2 (3d⁵ 4s¹): n = 5 ⟹ E_ex = [5(4)/2] K = 10K  (4K MORE STABLE!)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Exchange Energy ($E_{\text{ex}}$)**: The stabilizing energy released when electrons with parallel spins swap positions among degenerate orbitals:

$$\mathbf{E_{\text{ex}} = \frac{n(n-1)}{2} \cdot K}$$

where $n$ is the number of parallel-spin electrons and $K$ is the exchange constant.

**Anomalous Transition Metal Configurations**:
• **Chromium ($\text{Cr}, Z=24$)**: Predicted $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4 4s^2 \longrightarrow$ **Actual $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 4s^1$** ($10K$ exchange energy).
• **Copper ($\text{Cu}, Z=29$)**: Predicted $[\text{Ar}] 3d^9 4s^2 \longrightarrow$ **Actual $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^1$** ($20K$ exchange energy).
• **Palladium ($\text{Pd}, Z=46$)**: Predicted $[\text{Kr}] 4d^8 5s^2 \longrightarrow$ **Actual $[\text{Kr}] 4d^{10} 5s^0$** (**Double $s\rightarrow d$ shift** yielding closed-shell $4d^{10}$).
• **Other notable anomalous elements**: $\text{Nb} (4d^4 5s^1), \text{Mo} (4d^5 5s^1), \text{Ru} (4d^7 5s^1), \text{Rh} (4d^8 5s^1), \text{Ag} (4d^{10} 5s^1), \text{Pt} (5d^9 6s^1), \text{Au} (5d^{10} 6s^1)$.

quickRevision: Orbitals fill by (n+l) rule; if tied, lower n fills first.
Pauli principle limits orbital capacity to 2 electrons with opposite spins.
